pairs.definition: Principle that occupational exposure should be kept "as low as reasonably achievable."
The intensity of radiation is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.
A radiation worker's lifetime effective dose should not exceed 10 mSv times the person's age in years.
The radiation output weighted time that the unit is actually delivering radiation during the week.
The fraction of the work week during which the radiation beam is directed at a particular barrier.
Used to account for the fraction of the work week that a space beyond a barrier is occupied.
Prevents direct, or unscattered, radiation from reaching personnel or the public on the other side.
Consists of leakage radiation from the tube housing and scatter radiation from the patient.
Annual occupational effective dose limit for whole-body exposure.
Monthly allowable equivalent dose to the embryo-fetus from an occupationally exposed pregnant technologist.
